topic: Eight NVIDIA DGX Sparks clustered into 1 TB of unified memory running the GLM 5.3 753B frontier model
title: 8 DGX Sparks, 1 TB: frontier AI on a desk
description: Working description; the package stage overwrites this. Eight DGX Sparks now cluster into 1 TB of unified memory and run the full GLM 5.3 (753B) at about 470 GB in NVFP4. You'll learn what the cluster really buys: capacity, not speed. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: One terabyte of memory, on your desk.
Eight desk boxes now hold what a datacenter rents.
NVIDIA just blessed an eight-Spark cluster.
Your desk just got a terabyte of model memory.
A frontier model now runs on eight desk boxes.
Eight Sparks, one terabyte, one cable.
Eight DGX Sparks replaced the datacenter rental.
The four hundred seventy gigabyte file on a desk.
Eight little boxes, one frontier model, no cloud.
narration_full: One terabyte of memory just shrank to your desk. NVIDIA now supports linking eight DGX Sparks, desk-side AI computers, into one shared pool. Your gaming PC or Mac watched models this size from a browser tab. That pool runs G L M five point three, seven hundred fifty-three billion parameters. The whole model is one four hundred seventy gigabyte file on a desk. The catch: the cable between boxes is eleven times slower than the memory inside each one. You buy room, not speed. And yet it types at thirty-one tokens per second in NVIDIA's own test, no cloud account. The frontier moved from their building to your desk.

One text block animating at a time; amber accent underline draws under '1 TB' last 0.5 s.

Right panel: a horizontal memory bar in slab style fills with amber on 'four hundred seventy gigabyte file', '470 GB file' label above it. The bar fills once, no loop. Number lands with the amber fill; nothing else moves during the fill.

scenes.narration: The catch: the cable between boxes is eleven times slower than the memory inside each one. You buy room, not speed.
scenes.visual_brief: Centered stack: two slabs with a thin amber trace between them (the cable) above a wide lane inside one slab (its own memory). On 'eleven times slower' the cable trace flashes amber once while the inner lane stays solid: the contrast is the picture. On 'room, not speed' the cable trace dims and the pooled outline from s02 fades back in behind, still. At most two elements animate at once.

scenes.narration: And yet it types at thirty-one tokens per second in NVIDIA's own test, no cloud account. The frontier moved from their building to your desk.
scenes.visual_brief: Giant digits '31' with 'tokens/sec' beneath, same slab frame as frame 1 (rhyme). On 'NVIDIA's own test' a small chrome vendor tag fades in and out. On 'your desk' the digits settle and the amber underline returns under the number, then the wordmark settle takes the final 0.5 s. Video stops within a second of the last spoken word.

notes_for_review: Reviewer: 'eleven times slower' is the 196 Gb/s link vs 273 GB/s inside one Spark (brief claim 8, rounded); 'thirty-one tokens per second' is NVIDIA's vendor benchmark, attributed in the narration; the ~$55,600 cluster cost and the 816B/Q8 fit stay unspoken (Unverified). 'G L M five point three' is pre-spoken for the voice engine.
